# Process Folder Exceptions: Sending Certain Products Straight to a Folder

Most labs send their prints to a print controller through Process Routing, for example Darkroom Pro. Sometimes a few products need to go somewhere else entirely, such as a wide format RIP or another printer's hot folder.

**Process Folder Exceptions** handle this. You choose a product, and optionally the options that identify it (such as a paper type). Matching jobs are then copied straight into a folder you pick, instead of going to a controller.

---

## How it works

* **It's checked before your normal routing.** A job that matches an exception goes to the exception's folder, not to Process Routing or your Channel Mappings.
* **Files go straight into the folder.** Each image is copied loose into the folder you choose, not into a sub-folder, so a RIP or hot folder picks it up straight away. Files keep the name they were downloaded with, which usually already starts with the order number and job number, for example `PXDEMO-HTAR2U_38589203_Q1_pages9.jpeg`. If a name doesn't, the order number and job number are added to the front, so names never clash. If your RIP wants each job in a folder of its own, tick **Put each job in its own sub-folder** on the exception: each job then gets a folder named after its order and job number, with the files inside.
* **Nothing is ever overwritten.** If a file with the same name is already there, the new one gets **_2**, **_3** and so on added.
* **Your edits are used.** Crops and enhancements you made in Job Review are what get copied. Images you discarded are left out.
* **Reprints go to the same folder.** A reprint of a matched job is copied into the exception's folder, with **-r1**, **-r2** and so on in the file name, for example `PXDEMO-HTAR2U_38589203_Q1_pages9-r1.jpeg`.

---

## Adding an exception

1. Open OrderHub Desktop and go to **Settings → Routing → Process Folder Exceptions**.
2. Click **+ Add Exception**.
3. In **Product Code**, enter the product code exactly as it appears on the job, for example `0808-photo-print`.
   * Note: Capital letters and spaces at either end don't matter.
4. Optional: under **Options (name : value pairs)**, click **+ Add Option** and enter an option **name** and **value**, for example **Paper** : **Metallic**. Add as many as you need.
   * Note: A job matches only if it has **all** the options you list. It may have other options as well.
   * Note: With no options, every job with that product code matches.
5. In **Folder Path**, click **Browse...** and choose the folder the files should go to, for example your RIP's hot folder.
6. Tick **Auto Print** if matching jobs should be copied automatically as they arrive. Leave it unticked to copy them only when you click **Process**.
7. Click **Save Exception**.

![Settings for excepted jobs](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/aeaa55df-8063-472b-abd3-a09b25aff483.png)

To change or remove an exception, use **Edit** or **Delete** next to it in the list.

![Process Folder Exceptions](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/f90ac551-47bd-4256-aa24-37cc16f268d4.png)

---

## Sending the jobs

* **By hand:** open the job and click **Process**. The files are copied to the exception's folder.
* **Automatically:** with **Auto Print** ticked on the exception, matching jobs are copied as soon as they arrive.

Once the files are copied, the job is marked In Production — complete it in OrderHub once it's printed.

* Note: Ticking **Auto Print** only affects jobs that arrive from then on. It won't suddenly send every matching job that's already waiting; click **Process** to send those.

---

## Good to know

* **Your own choice wins.** If you reassign a job, or pick a different size with **Crop to Size**, in Job Review, that choice is used instead of the exception.
* **The first match is used.** If two exceptions match the same job, the one added first is used. Keep exceptions specific so only one can match.
* **The folder isn't watched.** OrderHub Desktop copies the files and its job is done. What happens next is up to the RIP or printer reading that folder.
